title: Adaptive Window Batch Stabilizer for Continuous Serving
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Introduce an adaptive sliding-window admission controller and batch stabilizer that smooths prefill/decode load spikes, improves p99 tail latency, and provides kernel-selection hints for heterogeneous batch shapes.
background: We continue to see rare but persistent p99 spikes on multi-tenant hosts when a small number of long-sequence prefill requests arrive concurrently with many short decode requests. Current admission logic uses static thresholds and per-tenant hard caps which either underutilize GPUs or allow tail events. Recent kernel-selection work shows significant variance in throughput depending on batch shape and sequence length distribution; however serving lacks a lightweight feedback loop to surface that info into admission decisions.
proposed_solution: Build 'Adaptive Window Batch Stabilizer' (AWBS) composed of three coordinated components: (1) a sliding admission window that tracks recent sequence-length histogram and arrival rate per host and tenant; (2) a batch shaper that enforces soft quotas and applies probabilistic hold-and-release to smooth spikes (percentile-based tail guard); (3) a kernel hinting API that exposes expected batch shape to the scheduler so it can pick kernels optimized for the imminent decode/prefill mix. The system uses exponential decay for historical weighting and a tunable aggressiveness factor per customer tier.
acceptance_criteria: p99 steady-state latency for mixed workload reduced by >= 20% in our internal benchmark cluster
no regression in throughput (tokens/sec) for 95th percentile scenarios (<5% change)
feature flag enables gradual rollout by host and can be toggled without restarts
observability: new dashboards showing sliding-window histograms, hold-rate, kernel-hint matches, and per-tenant soft-quota breaches
technical_notes: Admission window maintained in shared host memory with an atomic circular buffer summarizing sequence-length buckets. Batch shaper applies a cheap RNG-based hold for requests when the predicted tail probability exceeds threshold; held requests are prioritized in the next micro-batch. Kernel hinting uses a lightweight proto on the request path carrying expected max_seq and avg_seq to scheduler; scheduler returns a kernel_id suggestion. Ensure this path is non-blocking and falls back if kernel hint not honored. We will add a bounded token budget reservation for long prefill requests to avoid head-of-line surprises.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary on 2 small hosts with synthetic mixed workloads, feature flag off by default. 2) Enable for <5% of hosts in eu-west-1 for 48h, monitor p95/p99 and GPU occupancy. 3) Gradually increase to 50% with AB compare to control hosts. 4) Full rollout if metrics stable and no customer incidents. Rollback via feature flag within 1 minute.
risks: Mis-tuned aggressiveness could increase queueing and hurt p50 latency for latency-sensitive tenants
Kernel hint mismatch could cause suboptimal kernel picks and transient CPU-GPU underutilization
Complexity in cross-tenant fairness when some tenants opt-in to more aggressive smoothing
testing_plan: Unit tests for sliding-window state machine, integration tests with simulated scheduler that verifies kernel hints are passed and honored, load tests with our mixed-workload harness (short decodes + long prefill) to validate p99 improvements. Add chaos tests that randomly drop hints to ensure graceful fallback.
